name: Janani Jhumar

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: a patient, precise instructor who counts out loud, demonstrates from the front and the back, repeats every step slowly three times before speeding up, names mistakes kindly and never rushes
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

This is Janani Jhumar. Traditional.

Title card: Janani Jhumar · India · Traditional

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Janani Jhumar originates from the Chota Nagpur Plateau region of Jharkhand.
The dance is performed seasonally, starting in the month of Ashadh (June–July) and concluding in the month of Kartik (October–November).
on_screen: Map: India · South Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Janani Jhumar is performed during the festivals of Karam and Jitiya.
It marks the seasonal transition leading into the marriage season.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is women-centric.
Participants hold each other's hands in a linear line and move in a circular formation.
The movements are characterized by feminine grace.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (kV5bpXVlPBw)
Signature moves — MISSING
Formation: Women hold each other's hand, form a linear line and dance in a circle.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is provided by men playing the mandar, dhol, and bansi.
Women participate by singing while they dance.
Listen for the mandar, dhol, bansi.
The music features the rhythmic percussion of the mandar and dhol drums, accompanied by the melodic sound of the bansi flute, with vocal accompaniment provided by the dancers.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The dance is performed in open spaces during festivals like Karam and Jitiya.
When performed in a courtyard, the dance is specifically referred to as Angnai.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Variants include Purbaha, Pachhimaha, Uttaraha, Dakshinaha, Sonpuriya, Nagpuriya, Jashpuriya, Gangpuriya, Henthghatiya, and Assamiya.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Janani Jhumar (India). Instruments: mandar, dhol, bansi. Vocal style: Women sing while dancing.. Mood: graceful, festive. It should sound like this: The music features the rhythmic percussion of the mandar and dhol drums, accompanied by the melodic sound of the bansi flute, with vocal accompaniment provided by the dancers. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
